To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we propose a novel local correction for wide angle lenses based on a LUT built on a planar target.

(1) the proposed method is able to provide a local undistortion for fisheye cameras; (2) the method does not need any specific mathematical model for the lens distortion; (3) the method is able to work in real time; (4) the method is robust to different operating conditions.
we propose a new method for fisheye lens distortion correction, based on a local correction approach, that can be used as preliminary step for image elements recognition in images stitching.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and implementation of a novel distortion correction approach for wide angle and ultra-wide angle lenses.
a novel approach for fisheye lens undistortion based on a piecewise distortion correction of the target area.
the development of an efficient and accurate method to compensate for lens distortion in images taken from wide angle and fisheye lenses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed approach can be used as a first step for image undistortion, but also for image registration in the case of images acquired from a wide angle or ultra wide angle camera with a planar target in the field of view.
our proposed method is a fast and effective solution to the distortion correction problem for wide-angle fisheye lenses.

the proposed approach is a good solution to correct the image distortion locally, in particular in the case of low cost fisheye lenses, and that it is a good starting point to develop more sophisticated methods to correct the image in the peripheral regions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a global distortion model can be built by using a local approach.

the proposed approach is a local undistortion approach based on the LUT technique for a specific planar target region, where the LUT is built in order to minimize the interpolation and the residual distortion.
the proposed method can be considered as a local correction approach for fisheye images that can be applied to a large class of fisheye lens models.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the local distortion model can be applied in the case of low cost fisheye lenses and it can be considered as a preliminary step in image processing pipelines where a global undistortion is not required.

a simple local correction can provide a good approximation of the global distortion in the peripheral region of fisheye lenses and can be used in applications where a complete undistortion cannot be applied.
a local correction approach can be a good alternative to global distortion correction, in particular in the case of low quality images where global distortion correction is difficult to obtain.
